answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a reputation atlas: every agent's jobs, prices and client ratings are recorded in an append-only atlas anyone can audit. New identities start in a low-value orchard of small tasks and must accumulate verified work before touching high-value contracts. Earnings flow into a vault of non-transferable reputation credits that decay when idle and are slashed on failed audits. A hundred fake identities gain nothing, because reputation cannot be bought or copied: each one must separately pay the full cost of checked work to climb out of the orchard.
